h1: The 6 Best Lawn Mowers for Hills of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers for Hills 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six self-propelled, rear-wheel drive and robot mowers for sloped lawns, with the drive type and tradeoffs that matter on a hill.
summary: The EGO POWER+ 21-inch self-propelled kit is our top pick for a maintained hilly lawn. The Greenworks 80V is the better buy under $500, and the SENIX gas mower is the choice for variable-speed control. The Segway Navimow is the pick if you would rather not walk the slope at all.
intro: The usual hill mistake is buying a push mower and trusting your legs. On a slope a mower with no drive wheels feels twice as heavy, and the weight shifts back onto you with every uphill pass. Drive type matters more here than deck width or horsepower.

We reviewed six mowers on paper, comparing drive system, power source, deck size and what each is built to handle. We ranked them on the spec sheet and what owners report, not on timed slope runs, and show price as a bucket.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower Kit (LM2135SP)
products.verdict: A cordless self-propelled kit that takes the strain out of slopes.
products.description:
The EGO POWER+ is a 21-inch cordless self-propelled mower sold as a kit with battery and charger. It falls in the $500+ bucket and removes both gas and cord from the equation.

It ranks above the Greenworks because owners treat it as the more polished cordless option on a maintained hilly lawn, though it costs noticeably more. Compared with the gas SENIX below, you give up unlimited refueling but gain quiet starts and no maintenance.

Choose it if your lawn is hilly but groomed and you want hassle-free starts. The caveat is the battery, since a very large sloped yard may need a spare.
products.idealFor: Owners of a maintained hilly lawn who want cordless ease.
products.skipIf: You have a very large yard or want to spend under $500.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Self-propelled cordless power for much less than the EGO.
products.description:
The Greenworks is a 21-inch self-propelled mower on an 80V platform, supplied with a 4Ah battery and charger. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

Second comes down to this, since it gives you the same core hill benefit as the EGO, a driven wheel set, at a lower price. The tradeoff is that the EGO is the more premium cordless line.

It suits sloped residential lawns where you want cordless without the top-tier price. The caveat is the 4Ah battery, which limits runtime on a big or thick lawn.
products.idealFor: Residential slopes where cordless value matters most.
products.skipIf: You mow over half an acre on one charge.

products.name: Segway Navimow X430 Wire-Free Robot Mower
products.verdict: Skips the walking entirely with 4WD and wire-free navigation.
products.description:
The Segway Navimow X430 is a robot mower with wire-free navigation for up to 1 acre and 4WD that the manufacturer states for 84 percent slopes. It falls in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks third because it is a different kind of buy. It beats every walk-behind on effort, but it cannot clear thick or tall growth the way a push mower can, and it costs far more than the gas options.

It suits owners with an obstacle-clear sloped lawn who never want to push again. The caveat is that the slope rating is the manufacturer's claim, so treat it as a ceiling, not a guarantee.
products.idealFor: Obstacle-clear sloped lawns where you want hands-off mowing.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has many obstacles or gets very tall.

products.name: SENIX 201cc 22-Inch Variable Speed Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: A big gas engine with a drive speed you can dial in.
products.description:
The SENIX pairs a 201cc gas engine with a 22-inch deck and a variable-speed self-propelled drive. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

The fourth slot reflects that it is more powerful than the PowerSmart gas mowers below and lets you slow the drive on steep sections, but it is heavier and louder than the cordless trio above.

It suits owners who prefer gas runtime and want control over walking speed. The caveat is routine engine upkeep like oil and fuel, which cordless mowers avoid.
products.idealFor: Gas-mower fans who want adjustable walking pace.
products.skipIf: You want no fuel or oil maintenance.

products.name: PowerSmart 22-Inch 170cc Self-Propelled Gas Mower
products.verdict: Self-propelled traction on a moderate slope without the premium.
products.description:
The PowerSmart 22-inch uses a 170cc gas engine, a 22-inch deck and a self-propelled drive. It lands in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks fifth because it lacks the variable-speed control of the SENIX, so you walk at one pace. It is a step better than a push mower for moderate slopes though.

It suits budget buyers with a moderately sloped lawn. The caveat is that the single-speed drive can feel too quick or too slow depending on terrain.
products.skipIf: Your slopes are steep or you want speed control.

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch Rear-Wheel Drive Gas Mower for Hills
products.verdict: Rear-wheel drive that pushes from behind on a climb.
products.description:
This PowerSmart has a 170cc OHV engine, a 21-inch alloy steel deck and rear-wheel drive. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks last because the narrower deck means more passes, and the picks above offer more features. Rear-wheel drive is its real argument, since driving from the back keeps weight over the powered wheels going uphill.

Buy it if you want a gas mower built with slopes in mind. The caveat is the smaller deck, which adds time on a big lawn.
products.idealFor: Gas buyers who want rear-drive traction on slopes.
products.skipIf: You have a large lawn and want a wider deck.

whatMatters.detail: Self-propelled mowers power the wheels so you do not push the weight uphill. Rear-wheel drive keeps traction when climbing, while 4WD grips in several directions. Check the listing for the drive wording, not just a general 'powerful' claim.
Gas gives long runtime but needs oil and fuel. Cordless starts instantly and is quiet but is limited by battery capacity. Look for the battery size in Ah and decide against your lawn size.
A variable-speed drive lets you slow down on steep or uneven sections. A single-speed drive forces you to match its pace. The listing should say variable speed explicitly.
A 21 or 22 inch deck is a balance of coverage and handling. Wider decks finish faster but are harder to turn on slopes. Compare the inch figure with your lawn size.
Makers sometimes state a maximum slope angle or percentage. These are manufacturer figures and not independent tests. Treat them as an upper limit and stay well under it for safety.

howToChoose.intro: Drive type decides how much work the hill is.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: Gas has unlimited runtime if you refuel, but needs maintenance. The SENIX and both PowerSmart mowers are gas.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Cordless is quiet and easy to start, limited by battery. The EGO POWER+ and Greenworks fit this group.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to cordless unless the lawn is large.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Driven wheels, ideally rear or 4WD, plus variable speed so you can slow down on the steepest sections.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Segway Navimow X430 is the 4WD option, the PowerSmart RWD drives from behind, and the SENIX has variable speed.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You value cordless convenience or want to stop mowing manually, which points to the EGO POWER+ or Segway Navimow.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your slopes are moderate, where the PowerSmart 22-Inch gives you drive at the lowest price.

faq.q: Can I mow a steep hill safely with any mower?
faq.a: No. Mow across slopes with a push mower and up and down with a ride-on only if the manual says so. Always follow the maker's slope limit.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake on slopes?
faq.a: Buying a mower with no drive wheels. The weight falls on your arms and the climb tires you quickly.

faq.q: Is the EGO worth it over the Greenworks?
faq.a: Only if you want the more premium cordless line. The Greenworks delivers the same hill-friendly drive for less.

faq.q: Does the Segway need a boundary wire?
faq.a: The listing says wire-free navigation, so no. You still need a clear lawn without many obstacles.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas mower?
faq.a: Change the oil, check the air filter and use fresh fuel each season. Store it with the tank handled per the manual.

faq.q: Can a robot handle tall grass?
faq.a: Robots are made for regular trims, not for thick or overgrown lawns. Keep the grass short for best results.

finalTake: The EGO POWER+ is the best all-round hill mower here. The Greenworks gives most of the benefit for less money, and the SENIX is the gas pick with speed control. The Segway Navimow is the right buy only if automated mowing appeals. Whatever you choose, make sure the drive is powered.
